item.title: Finiteness of local cohomology modules over arbitrary regular local rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.10064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider arbitrary regular local ring $S$ and an ideal $J\subset S$ whose minimal primes are cohomologically complete intersection. Using the Mayer-Vietoris spectral sequence, in Section 2, we construct examples of local cohomology modules $H^i_J (S)$, whose set of associated primes is finite. As a special case we show that the set of associated primes $H^i_J (S)$ is finite when minimal primes of $J$ are part of a specific regular system of parameters and satisfy a `Dropping Condition'. In Section 3, we prove Theorem 2.3 along with its asssociated corollary in a more general setting, without the use of `Dropping Condition'. These examples of local cohomology modules include the cases whose associative primes also can contain prime number $p$.
item.dc:creator: Rajsekhar Bhattacharyya

item.title: A divisorial domain with non-Pr\"ufer normalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.11357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We answer a 1968 question of Heinzer by constructing a two-dimensional local divisorial domain whose normalization is not Pr\"ufer.
item.dc:creator: Viet-Hoang Tran

item.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
item.description: arXiv:2611.12008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gr\"obner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.
item.dc:creator: Tran Nam Trung, Hoang Le Truong

item.title: Split Kernel Multiplication Modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.12320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce split kernel multiplication (SKM) modules, for which every submodule has the form $N=IM\oplus\ker f$, where $I$ is an ideal of $R$ and $f$ is an endomorphism of $M$. We study direct sums, localization, and connections with multiplication and retractability properties. For the idempotent version (ISKM), we prove that $R\oplus k^b$ is ISKM over a local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$, with residue field $k$ and $b\geq1$, if and only if $\mathfrak m^2=0$. We also classify ISKM modules of the form $R^a\oplus k^b$ over local rings. For commutative Noetherian rings, we show that $R^2$ is SKM if and only if $R$ is an Artinian principal ideal ring. Finally, we prove that every finitely generated $R$-module is ISKM if and only if $R$ is a finite product of fields.
item.dc:creator: Violeta Leoreanu-Fotea, \"Unsal Tekir, Dilara Erdemir

item.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.
item.dc:creator: Veronika Kikteva

item.title: The Gorsky-Oblomkov-Rasmussen conjecture over $\mathbb{Q}$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10885v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a generation theorem for the homology of certain Koszul complexes which naturally arise as the $E^1$ pages of the stable Rasmussen spectral sequence of torus links. Combining this theorem with recent work of Ballinger, Gorsky, Hogancamp, and Wang, we compute the stable Khovanov-Rozansky $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ homology of torus links and determine its Poincar\'e series, resolving conjectures of Gorsky, Oblomkov, and Rasmussen and their $\mathfrak{gl}_N$ analogs, over $\mathbb{Q}$. Using these results, we determine the Khovanov homology of $T(n,n-1)$ and $T(n,n)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, confirming conjectures of Shumakovitch and Turner and of the first author, which in turn allows us to compute the Khovanov skein lasagna module of $\overline{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$.
item.dc:creator: Qiuyu Ren, Hongjian Yang

item.title: Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.12289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula. The proof expresses the Tjurina defect through multiplication in the filtered Milnor algebra and uses the monomial strong Lefschetz theorem to attain the resulting rank bound. We also determine the associated graded higher Tjurina algebras of this family and show that they are unchanged by terms of order at least $m+2$.
item.dc:creator: Chuangqiang Hu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Lishan Yu, Huaiqing Zuo

item.title: The Frobenius Problem for Generalized Repunit Numerical Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2112.01106v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce and study the numerical semigroups generated by $\{a_1, a_2, \ldots \} \subset \mathbb{N}$ such that $a_1$ is the repunit number in base $b > 1$ of length $n > 1$ and $a_i - a_{i-1} = a\, b^{i-2},$ for every $i \geq 2$, where $a$ is a positive integer relatively prime with $a_1$. These numerical semigroups generalize the repunit numerical semigroups among many others. We show that they have interesting properties such as being homogeneous and Wilf. Moreover, we solve the Frobenius problem for this family, by giving a closed formula for the Frobenius number in terms of $a, b$ and $n$, and compute other usual invariants such as the Ap\'ery sets, the genus or the type.
item.dc:creator: Manuel B. Branco, Isabel Cola\c{c}o, Ignacio Ojeda

item.title: Universally free numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2303.06474v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A numerical semigroup is said to be universally free if it is free for any possible arrangement of its minimal generating set. In this work, we establish that toric ideals associated with universally free numerical semigroups can be generated by their set of circuits. Additionally, we provide a characterization of universally free numerical semigroups in terms of Gr\"obner bases. Specifically, a numerical semigroup is universally free if and only if all initial ideals of its corresponding toric ideal are complete intersections. Furthermore, we establish several equalities among the toric bases of a universally free numerical semigroup. We provide a complete characterization of $3$-generated universally free numerical semigroups in terms of their minimal generating sets, and by proving the equality of certain toric bases. We compute exactly all the toric bases of a toric ideal defined by a 3-generated universally free numerical semigroup. Notably, we answer some questions posed by Tatakis and Thoma by demonstrating that toric ideals defined by $3$-generated universally free numerical semigroups have a set of circuits and a universal Gr\"obner basis of size 3, while the universal Markov basis and the Graver basis can be arbitrarily large. We present partial results and propose several conjectures regarding universally free numerical semigroups with more than three generators.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra 228 (2024), 107551
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Garc\'ia Marco, Pedro A. Garc\'ia-S\'anchez, Ignacio Ojeda, Christos Tatakis

item.title: On the depth of simplicial affine semigroup rings
item.description: arXiv:2307.16501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We recall and delve into the different characterizations of the depth of an affine semigroup ring, providing an original characterization of depth two in three and four dimensional cases which are closely related to the existence of a maximal element in certain Apery sets.
item.dc:creator: Raheleh Jafari, Ignacio Ojeda

item.title: Arithmetic varieties of numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2311.13500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we present the notion of arithmetic variety for numerical semigroups. We study various aspects related to these varieties such as the smallest arithmetic that contains a set of numerical semigroups and we exhibit the root three associated with an arithmetic variety. This tree is not locally finite; however, if the Frobenius number is fixed, the tree has finitely many nodes and algorithms can be developed. All algorithms provided in this article include their (non-debugged) implementation in GAP.
item.dc:creator: Manuel B. Branco, Ignacio Ojeda, Jos\'e Carlos Rosales

item.title: Cellular free resolutions for normalizations of toric ideals
item.description: arXiv:2512.17871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any toric ideal $I$ in a polynomial ring $S$, we provide a combinatorial description of a free resolution of the integral closure of the $S$-module $S/I$. These new complexes arise from an extension of Bayer--Sturmfels' theory of cellular free resolutions. As applications, we unify several constructions for a resolution of the diagonal embedding of a toric variety, and compare the locally free resolutions for toric subvarieties introduced by Hanlon--Hicks--Lazarev and Brown--Erman.
item.dc:creator: Christine Berkesch, Lauren Cranton Heller, Gregory G. Smith, Jay Yang

item.title: Generators of the initial ideal of simplicial toric ideals
item.description: arXiv:2603.07488v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe a generating set for the initial ideal of simplicial toric ideals with respect to the graded reverse lexicographic order, using representations of elements of affine monoids as sums of irreducible elements. Although the resulting generating set is not necessarily minimal, we demonstrate, through an example, how one can obtain the reduced Gr\"obner basis from it. Moreover, we compare the maximal degree of the Gr\"obner basis and the Castelnuvo-Mumford regularity.
item.dc:creator: Ryotaro Hanyu

item.title: On $S$-Noetherian Lattices
item.description: arXiv:2604.26058v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we define and study $S$-Noetherian lattices as a natural generalization of Noetherian rings. We prove that a ring $R$ is $S$-Noetherian if and only if its ideal lattice, $Id(R)$, is $S_L$-Noetherian. Furthermore, we establish a Cohen-Kaplansky type theorem for $S$-Noetherian lattices, showing that $L$ is $S$-Noetherian if and only if every $S$-prime element of $L$ is $S$-compact. Finally, we introduce the concept of $S$-primary elements - a generalization of primary elements in multiplicative lattices and demonstrate the existence (when every element of $S$ is meet principal, as is the case for the ideal lattice of a ring) and uniqueness of $S$-primary decomposition in $S$-Noetherian lattices.
item.dc:creator: Sachin Sarode, Chetan Patil, Vinayak Joshi

item.title: Non-Noetherian Bass and Betti numbers
item.description: arXiv:2606.20391v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates the vanishing and non-vanishing of Betti and Bass numbers for non-finitely generated modules. We prove that for $d$-dimensional Cohen--Macaulay local rings, every non-zero $\mathfrak{m}$-torsion module satisfies $\beta_d(M)\neq 0$, and we establish the Betti number behavior of the injective hull $E_R(k)$. We study tor-rigidity for $H^d_{\mathfrak{m}}(R)$. We also provide positive answer to Schoutens' question on whether the vanishing of some Betti number of a big Cohen--Macaulay algebra forces the Cohen--Macaulay property of $R$. For the absolute integral closure $R^+$, we establish both Tor and Ext results. On the Tor side, we prove that $\beta_i(R^+)=0$ for some $i>0$ implies regularity in a series cases. On the Ext side, we prove that $\mu_i(R^+)=0$ for some $i> d$ forces regularity for Gorenstein domains of prime characteristic, and we obtain analogous results for graded normal domains of dimension $2$ and also for quotient and isolated singularities in any dimension. Also $\mu_i(R^\infty)=0$ forces regularity for isolated singularity.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh, Elham Mahdavi

item.title: On the linearity of squarefree powers of edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2607.00838v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be a graph and $I(G)$ its edge ideal. The $p$-th squarefree power $I(G)^{[p]}$ is the monomial ideal generated by the squarefree monomials corresponding to the matchings of size $p$ of $G$. A central highlight of our work is the complete solution of a problem posed by Bigdeli, Herzog and Zaare-Nahandi in 2017, which asked to characterize when squarefree powers of edge ideals have the first syzygy module generated by linear forms. Moreover, for a $1$-dimensional flag simplicial complex $\Delta$ and its Stanley--Reisner ideal $I_\Delta$, which is the edge ideal of the complement graph of $\Delta$, we prove that $I_\Delta^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution if and only if it is linearly related and the $(2p-1)$-st homology of the neighbourhood complex of $\Delta$ vanishes. As a consequence, we describe the shape of the Betti table of $I_\Delta^{[p]}$, and we give a combinatorial characterization of when $I_\Delta^{[p]}$ has a linear resolution, provided that the $2p$-core of $\Delta$ has maximum degree at most $2p$. Finally, we show that no such characterization exists in general: the linearity of $I_\Delta^{[2]}$ may depend on the characteristic of the field, and it cannot be described by finitely many forbidden induced subgraphs.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Naoki Terai

item.title: Square-difference factorization: ring structure, torsion splitting, and ideal classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20884v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce and study commutative rings whose regular ideals, or all ideals, factor into square-difference factor absorbing ideals. We establish permanence under finite products, suitable localizations and quotients, and coefficient descent for monoid algebras. For an SP-domain, the regular factorization property is equivalent to the localization obtained by inverting $2$ being zero or Dedekind; equivalently, the maximal ideals avoiding $2$ are invertible and form a discrete subspace in the inverse topology. Over an arbitrary domain, we characterize unique functorial splitting of localization on all torsion modules by a condition excluding nonzero prime chains across the vanishing set of the localized element. Complementary localizations of one-dimensional Pr\"ufer domains give a decomposition of invertible ideal groups and an exact Picard-group sequence. For an SP-domain whose Picard group has finite exponent $m$, every irreducible element has local valuation at most $m$. We also give regular-ideal criteria for arbitrary idealizations and a complete strong-factorization criterion over von Neumann regular bases. The zero ideal is treated separately throughout, and explicit examples show why unrestricted quotient and localization assertions fail.
item.dc:creator: Malik Tusif Ahmed, Ahmed Hamed, Hafnaoui Hidouri, Hwankoo Kim

item.title: Intersection multiplicity of a sparse curve and a trinomial curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.35037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let f $\in$ C[x, y] be a trinomial and let g $\in$ C[x, y] be a sparse polynomial with N monomials (N $\ge$ 1). We address the problem of bounding the local intersection multiplicity of the bivariate polynomial system f = g = 0 at an isolated root q $\in$ (C * )^ 2 only in terms of N . Our main result establishes that the local multiplicity of the system at any isolated solution q $\in$ (C * ) ^2 is at most (N -1)(N +2)/ 2 , independently of the degrees of f and g. Furthermore, we know that this bound is sharp for N = 3.
item.dc:creator: Jean Mousseau (LAMA)

item.title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.41659v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound. A connection to (generalized) Loewy length is given.
item.dc:creator: Mohsen Asgharzadeh

item.title: Leaf-discriminating trees for multiparameter counting of numerical semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2607.23111v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid of ${\mathbb N}$. The largest element of the complement is its {\em Frobenius number} and the cardinality of its complement is the {\em genus}. We propose a new approach to counting semigroups by the Frobenius number and by the genus, by introducing two ad-hoc trees. Those are leaf-discriminating trees in the sense that their leaves correspond exactly to the objects we want to count and, so, exploring these trees instead of general trees is optimal. Our approach reduces the search space for genus to 23\% and for Frobenius to 0.03\% of that required by previous approaches and this allowed to obtain an important number of unkown terms from both sequences. We implemented a recursive descending algorithm based on the so-called seeds structure, trimming the general semigroup tree exactly at those nodes with no descendants with a given genus, in the first case, or with no descendants with a given Frobenius number, in the second case. We refined the parallelizing strategies and we overcame the previous limitation of the length of integers in the bitwise representation of the gap sequence and the seed sequence. We computed multiparameter decomposition of the numbers of semigroups of each Frobenius number up to $135$, the number of irreducible semigroups of Frobenius number up to $135$, and of the numbers of semigroups of each genus up to $80$.
item.dc:creator: Maria Bras-Amor\'os, Vicen\c{c} Torra

item.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
item.description: arXiv:2608.01474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkan\'e to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}
item.dc:creator: Jean Kabor\'e, Ibrahim Nonkan\'e

item.title: Common zeros of homogeneous polynomials and the weight hierarchy of projective Reed-Muller codes
item.description: arXiv:2611.08203v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the maximum number of common zeros in projective space of any set of linearly independent homogeneous polynomials of the same degree, when the degree is smaller than the cardinality of the finite field. This proves the conjecture of Beelen, Datta, and Ghorpade, resolving a longstanding problem on common zeros and determining the complete weight hierarchy of the corresponding projective Reed-Muller codes. The proof uses Green's hyperplane restriction bound, combined with a footprint argument that reduces the problem to the affine case solved by Heijnen and Pellikaan. Wei duality then determines the hierarchy in sufficiently large degrees, recovering the complete hierarchy in every degree for the projective plane. Finally, we prove an upper bound valid in every degree, and conjecture that it is always sharp.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo San-Jos\'e
